summary: REQUEST_CHANGES on PR #334 exact head 3475ca65f86e1dbb63e0d4d985ca5e4b3fd7c625, superseding this worker's earlier source PASS/HOLD. The returned PhysicsLabRuntime facade exposes mutable registry/fidelity authority capabilities and transaction fields, so transition callbacks can bypass the public step/dispose guard and mutate authority state directly. No Studio evidence was run or claimed.
evidence: PhysicsLabRuntime.new() returns a mutable table containing _registry, _fidelity, _entityIds, _disposed, and _transitionInFlight; assertMutationAllowed only mediates public step() and dispose().

WorldEntity.createRegistry().unregister() immediately removes a registered record through the leaked _registry capability. An observeTransition callback can capture the runtime, unregister an unrelated entity, return normally, and let the target transition continue while FidelityManager still retains the unrelated registration.

Direct writes to _transitionInFlight can also defeat the public mutation fence. A frozen facade would still be insufficient if mutable registry/fidelity capabilities remain reachable; the authority handles and transaction state must be closure-private/opaque.
